study_identification_part.si4_title: Cortical thickness and grey-matter volume anomaly detection in individual MRI scans: Comparison of two methods

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To compare the performance of ScanOMetrics (an open-source tool for detection of statistical anomalies in individual MRI scans) using metrics derived from two brain morphometry software tools (DL+DiReCT and FreeSurfer) in the context of normative modeling for Alzheimer's disease (AD) detection, and to assess whether the faster DL+DiReCT method provides evaluation metrics consistent with the widely-used FreeSurfer tool.

nm2_modeling_method.answer: Polynomial regression (low-order polynomials with adaptive degree selection)
nm2_modeling_method.reason: The paper clearly describes using low-order polynomial regression with adaptive degree selection based on nested F-tests. The polynomial degree was gradually increased from zero until no further statistical improvement was observed, with a maximum degree constraint to avoid overfitting.
nm2_modeling_method.supporting_text: In brief, low order polynomials were fitted to the 100 resamples of the SBA metrics of our HCs as a function of age. The degrees of the fit polynomials were adapted for each of the resamples separately by increasing from zero until the reduction of residual variance became insignificant (nested F tests). To exclude overfitting, the maximum degree was set as the odd number 2*floor(ln(n/10) + 1)-1, where n is the available number of samples... For example, when using all 1′927 scans with CDR = 0, the maximal allowed degree was 11.

Strengths include: (1) uniform age sampling to mitigate non-uniform age distributions, (2) iterative outlier removal to reduce impact of artifacts and poor quality scans, (3) covariate matching for sex/scanner/protocol, (4) incorporation of measurement uncertainty from repeated scans. clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of deviation patterns between AD and HC groups (effect size calculation using Cohen's d); Stratified analysis by CDR level (CDR=0.5, CDR=1, CDR≥2) to assess progression of atrophy patterns; ROC curve analysis with AUC calculation to evaluate classification performance (AD vs HC) based on: (1) percentage of abnormal metrics per scan, (2) signed log10(p) of entorhinal CTh, (3) signed log10(p) of hippocampal volume; Normalized L2-distance calculations between individual significance maps and group average templates to quantify pattern similarity; Correlation analysis (Pearson r=0.87) between DL+DiReCT and FreeSurfer L2-distances; Within-subject reproducibility assessment using L2-distances between repeated scans (Wilcoxon rank-sum test); Comparison of average cortical thickness change maps in converters (CDR=0 to CDR≥0.5); Binomial tests for outlier detection rates; Shapiro-Wilk tests for normality of fit residues; No explicit correction for multiple comparisons in regional anomaly detection (threshold set at p<0.01 uncorrected)
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Regardless of software used (DL+DiReCT or FreeSurfer), AD patients showed up to 20-fold more frequent cortical thickness anomalies than healthy controls, with detections mainly in known AD predilection areas (entorhinal cortex, fusiform gyrus, precuneus, supramarginal gyrus), and atrophy patterns extended with increasing clinical dementia rating; DL+DiReCT provided results more than 15 times faster than FreeSurfer.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: In established AD (CDR≥1), both DL+DiReCT and FreeSurfer identified 56-62% of scans as anomalous (>5% abnormal metrics), compared to only 0.8-1% in cleaned HCs, representing a ~20-fold difference. Regional cortical thickness (CTh) reductions were detected with strong bilateral preference in: entorhinal cortex (up to 28% of AD scans), fusiform gyrus, precuneus, and supramarginal gyrus, with frontal lobe least affected. ROC analysis for scan classification (AD vs HC) yielded AUCs of 0.76 (DL+DiReCT) and 0.72 (FreeSurfer) based on percentage of abnormal metrics, and both achieved AUC=0.75 for entorhinal CTh and hippocampal volume metrics. Progression with CDR was evident: using DL+DiReCT, abnormal entorhinal CTh was detected in 24.8% of CDR=0.5 cases, 47.2% of CDR=1, and 46.0% of CDR≥2 cases (FreeSurfer: 17.6%, 30.2%, 32.0% respectively). Individual anomaly patterns were highly heterogeneous (normalized L2-distances between individual maps and CDR≥2 template ranged widely, with correlation r=0.87 between DL+DiReCT and FreeSurfer), but group-averaged anomaly maps strongly resembled effect size maps from direct AD vs HC comparisons (Cohen's d). Within-subject reproducibility (L2-distance between rescans) was significantly better for DL+DiReCT than FreeSurfer in both AD (0.39±0.26 vs 0.44±0.24, p=0.05) and HC groups. In converters (CDR 0→≥0.5), average CTh reduction up to 0.1mm was observed in temporo-basal regions (entorhinal, parahippocampal, fusiform, inferior temporal gyrus), equivalent to 25 years of healthy aging. Individual hippocampal atrophy rate reached ~6%/year with DL+DiReCT (3.3%/year with FreeSurfer). Processing times: DL+DiReCT 24±5 minutes vs FreeSurfer 9h20m±2h50m (~15x faster). Strong correlation was found with other normative tools: PCN toolkit z-scores (r=0.98-0.99, p<1e-12) and BrainChart centiles (Spearman ρ=0.95, p<1e-12).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Single-site dataset from OASIS3 (all Siemens scanners, limited to 1.5T and 3T) may limit generalizability; No explicit harmonization beyond covariate matching; Non-normal residual distributions persisted (84-90% of metrics failed Shapiro-Wilk tests even after cleaning); Classification performance modest (AUC 0.72-0.76) insufficient for standalone diagnostic use; DL+DiReCT provides limited metrics compared to FreeSurfer's comprehensive output; Heterogeneous atrophy patterns in AD make individual-level classification challenging; Validation limited to same dataset (no external independent cohort); Measurement uncertainty estimates based on age-proximate rescans (within 10% age) may overestimate true uncertainty compared to same-session rescans
caa10_key_limitations.location: Romascano2024.pdf.md: Introduction, Section 2.4. Normative modeling, Section 3.7. Cleaning the normative models, Section 4.3. Value for clinical decision support, and Section 4.4. DL+DiReCT vs. FreeSurfer
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Since MRI acquisition settings like scanner type (Sinnecker et al., 2022) or scanning protocol (Rebsamen et al., 2023b) have been demonstrated to influence SBA estimates, control for these confounders by harmonization procedures is required... Shapiro-Wilk tests indicated that almost all metrics had non-normally distributed fit residues, with only minor improvements due to the cleaning procedures (decrease from 91 % to 85 % for DL + DiReCT and from 90 % to 84 % for FreeSurfer regarding the 358 raw metrics)... classifying entire scans as anomalous based on a threshold on the accepted rate of abnormal metrics is not sufficiently reliable... both approaches lead to areas under the ROC curve below 0.8, without greater difference between the evaluated software tools... DL + DiReCT's output is drastically reduced, currently focusing on some of the most frequently used SBA metrics... this estimate yields only an upper bound of the true uncertainty

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study emphasizes that automated anomaly detection should serve as a trigger for secondary inspection by human experts rather than as an automated disease classification tool, providing screening functionality to support neuroradiological assessment. Comparison to commercial tools (CE-marked, FDA-approved) is discussed, noting that clinical validation remains an open research topic despite formal approval. The study provides open-source implementation (ScanOMetrics on GitHub) with complete reproducibility via public data (OASIS3), online tutorials, and published normative models. Future directions include: combining normative residues with proportional hazard models for AD conversion prediction, multi-kernel classifiers, disease progression models; addressing heterogeneity across dementia subtypes and early vs late onset patterns; clinical evaluation studies with QReports (quantitative reports) similar to those conducted for hippocampal sclerosis in epilepsy; development of disease-specific QReports with graphical user interface.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is a methodological comparison study between two brain morphometry tools (DL+DiReCT vs FreeSurfer) within the ScanOMetrics normative modeling framework, applied to Alzheimer's disease detection. The study used 1,927 HC scans (696 participants) from OASIS3 for initial model building, with 99 scans (5.15%) removed after LOOCV cleaning, resulting in final models based on 1,828 scans. The clinical evaluation included 209 scans with CDR≥1 and additional analyses of CDR=0.5 cases (309 scans) and converters (87 scans from 41 subjects). Both tools extracted 358 raw metrics (GMV, mean CTh, SD of CTh) plus 239 ICV-normalized metrics (total 597) from the Desikan-Killiany atlas. The normative modeling used polynomial regression with adaptive degree selection (max degree 11 for this dataset size) and 100-fold uniform age resampling. Key technical features: two-stage outlier removal (1.5 IQR threshold), measurement uncertainty estimation from repeated scans, covariate matching for sex/scanner/protocol, and signed log10(p) values as deviation metric. Both tools showed similar regional detection patterns matching known AD pathology, but DL+DiReCT had slightly higher sensitivity (particularly for entorhinal cortex across CDR levels) and better scan-rescan reproducibility, while being ~15x faster (24 minutes vs 9.3 hours). The study did not find universally narrower residual distributions for DL+DiReCT (only 56 of 240 normalized metrics showed this, predominantly thickness measures; volumes favored FreeSurfer). Comparison to PCN toolkit and BrainChart showed strong agreement despite different modeling approaches and reference datasets. The paper notes that grouping subtypes with different atrophy patterns might impair accuracy while splitting into too many groups reduces statistical power. Hardware used: Dell Precision 7920 with dual Intel Xeon Gold 6148 CPUs (40 cores total), 256GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 GPU.
